# mas-router-method

A native-agent product for TikTok brand content: give it a viral reference video and
a brand, get back a **recipe** — a cloneable abstraction of that video, re-skinned
for the brand, structured enough for a shooter to act on.

Two surfaces: a **bot** in Feishu where the work happens, and a **workbench** where
the work is supervised.

## Status

Early. The runtime and schemas work; the two applications are manifests. See
`docs/roadmap.md` for what is being built and why, and `CLAUDE.md` for the current
state stated plainly.

## Start here

- `docs/product/thesis.md` — what this is for and the bet behind it
- `docs/roadmap.md` — what is next, ordered by risk
- `CLAUDE.md` — architecture, commands, and the constraints that are not obvious
- `GLOSSARY.md` — the vocabulary; use these words exactly

## Repo shape

```
apps/workbench      Next.js operator surface (recipe review, run inspection)
apps/bot-gateway    Feishu event gateway
packages/core       agent runtime, tool contracts, budget enforcement
packages/shared     Zod schemas — the only place a domain type is defined
packages/feishu     Feishu API adapter
packages/evals      eval harness and the cases themselves
docs/               thesis, ADRs, eval design, roadmap
```

## Setup

Requires Node 22+ and pnpm 12.

```bash
pnpm install
cp .env.example .env    # fill ANTHROPIC_API_KEY at minimum
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
```

`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is required for anything that runs the agent. Unit tests and
typechecks do not need it.

## Development process

This repo vendors its engineering process into `.claude/skills/` and adds an
agent-product flow on top. Start with `/native-agent-dev`; it routes to the right
stage. Provenance and upgrade steps for the vendored skills are in
`.claude/skills/VENDOR.md`.

The one rule worth repeating: **the eval set is the spec.** A spec without eval
cases is a wish, and every later argument about quality becomes an opinion.

## Main agent (capability-graph consultant)

`apps/bot-gateway` now hosts **Main**, a capability-graph consultant for data-product
and Agent Native builder questions. It answers in Feishu groups with a grounded
answer contract: conclusion, location, evidence, next actions, boundaries.

- Engine: `packages/consult` — 17 capability nodes, 14 problem routes, BM25 retrieval,
  grounded answers, optional model synthesis.
- Surface: `apps/bot-gateway` — Feishu long connection (default) or webhook.
- Graph and acceptance criteria: `docs/product/main-agent-capability-graph.md`.
- Knowledge snapshot: `packages/consult/data/sources.json`, produced by
  `python3 scripts/materialize-main-knowledge.py`.

```bash
pnpm --filter @mas/bot-gateway check   # read-only doctor: token, bot, scopes, sample answer
pnpm --filter @mas/bot-gateway dev     # long-connection gateway
```

For first-time Feishu setup, run `python3 scripts/feishu-onboard.py`, open the
printed link in Feishu, and confirm. The script then sets the event subscription
to long-connection mode and adds `im.message.receive_v1`.

# Agent Native Builder

一套给**不会写代码的产品开发者**用的方法。七阶段闭环、七个检查、四页文档。

## 这是什么，不是什么

**是**：让你能判断「agent 做出来的东西是不是真的能用」的一套动作。
**不是**：教你写代码。代码由 agent 写。

这个区别是整个方法的前提。不写代码的人不缺代码，缺的是判断——面对一个正在运行的东西，不知道哪里会坏、坏了看不出来、好了也不确定。

## 四页文档

| 文档 | 什么时候看 |
|---|---|
| `failure-atlas.html` | 看到「全部通过」但心里没底时（六类信号 + 七问句 + 四质量问句 + 附录） |
| `decision-tree.html` | 不知道下一步做什么时 |
| `terms.html` | 报告里出现看不懂的词时 |
| `atlas-test-report.html` | 想知道这套方法自己的证据时 |

## 七阶段

需求 → 设计 → 能跑 → **能判断** → 能交付 → 运营 → 迭代

「能判断」是唯一的硬门：判断标准建不起来，不要往下做。其余都可以回头。

**设计阶段从来没有方法论**，ANB 原来从「想法」直接跳到「能跑」。现在补上了 `anb-design` 的四问：
流程形状（固定 / 需临场判断，判断点几处）、拒绝清单（具体输入 → 必须改做什么）、
动作权限（按能不能撤销分三档）、交接契约（每个工具三行，第二行「什么时候别用」）。
答案落成 `work/designs/D-xxx`，`work check` 会校验四块是否齐全。

## Skill 包

`.claude/skills/anb*` 共 16 个：

- **`anb`** — 路由。你说「不知道下一步做什么」或「感觉不对」，它定位到一步或一个检查。
- **七个阶段** — `anb-idea`、`anb-design`、`anb-runnable`、`anb-judgeable`、`anb-shipable`、`anb-observable`、`anb-reusable`。每个以「这一步的验收是什么」开场，答不出来不许往下。
- **七个检查** — `anb-check-break`（故意弄坏）、`anb-check-offline`（断网）、`anb-check-readback`（逐条念）、`anb-check-otherdevice`（换设备）、`anb-check-output`（看三个真实输出）、`anb-check-reconcile`（把总数拆开加一遍）。

## 证据

这套方法不是推演出来的，是从一个真实项目里挖出来的。六个事故全部可查：

- `packages/core/src/run-agent.ts` — 预算检查恒假、截断超限
- `packages/evals/src/rules.ts` — 护栏把崩溃当通过
- `packages/evals/src/fixtures.ts` — 假环境比真环境宽松
- `packages/feishu/src/events.ts` — @ 判定认错人

另外有一个自测样本：`anb-experiment-linkdigest/`（403 行源码、358 行测试、31 个检查全过），它就是「机制全绿但产出不可用」的活例子——`node test/run-tests.js` 可复现。

## 已知不足

- 六步是按「能拦下什么错误」切的，不是按真实使用数据切的。
- 「故意弄坏」这个动作在非工程师身上还没验证过，可能有心理阻力。
- 模板仓库还没做——它必须从一个真实跑通的产品里长出来，目前没有。

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

A native-agent product for TikTok brand content. The agent takes a viral reference
video and produces a **Recipe**: a cloneable abstraction of that video, re-skinned
for one brand, structured enough that a shooter can act on it.

Two surfaces, deliberately separate:

- **`apps/workbench`** — the operator surface. Reviewing recipes, inspecting runs,
  editing brand guardrails, reading eval scores. Next.js App Router + Feishu OAuth.
- **`apps/bot-gateway`** — the Feishu surface, where the actual work happens. Meets
  users in the chat they already use.

Both call the same runtime. They differ only in how a request arrives and where
the result goes.

## Commands

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev                # turbo: all packages that define `dev`
pnpm typecheck          # turbo: tsc --noEmit across the workspace
pnpm test               # turbo: vitest (unit/integration — never calls a model)
pnpm lint
pnpm format

# One package
pnpm --filter @mas/core typecheck
pnpm --filter @mas/core test

# One test file, one test
cd packages/core && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/run-agent.test.ts
cd packages/core && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run -t "keeps a thrown error"

# Evals — these call the real model and cost money. Not part of `pnpm test`.
pnpm --filter @mas/evals eval
pnpm --filter @mas/evals eval -- --case <id>
```

Package scripts are invoked through `pnpm --filter <name> <script>`; every package
defines `typecheck`, `build`, `test`, `clean`.

## Architecture

### The dependency direction is one-way

```
apps/workbench ─┐
                ├─→ packages/core ─→ packages/shared
apps/bot-gateway┘         │
                          └─→ packages/feishu
packages/evals ──────────→ packages/core, packages/shared
```

`packages/shared` imports nothing from this repo. It is the schema layer — the
single place where a domain object is defined. If two packages need the same type,
it belongs there; a second definition is a bug that only surfaces after a schema
change.

The same rule applies to seed data: the four brand profiles live in
`packages/core/src/seed/brands.ts`, not in the eval fixtures. `evals` depends on
`core`, so a second copy in the fixtures would drift the moment a guardrail
changes — and the guardrails are exactly what the `should_fail` cases are built
on.

### `packages/core` is the whole product in one loop

`run-agent.ts` owns the agent loop: model call, step recording, budget enforcement,
cancellation, cost accounting. It is deliberately one file. Everything an agent
product must get right happens in *one* loop, and splitting that loop across
modules is how the budget check ends up not running on the path that matters.

`index.ts` composes it: `createRuntime()` wires the tools into an in-process MCP
server, sets the system prompt, and hands back a single `run()` method. Both apps
call that.

### Tools are defined against ports, not clients

`tools/brand.ts` declares interfaces (`BrandStore`, `ReferenceStore`, `RecipeStore`,
`VisionAnalyzer`) and builds the MCP tools against them. Production passes real
implementations; the eval harness passes fakes. The tool's prompt-visible contract
is identical in both, which is what makes agent behaviour testable without a live
Feishu tenant.

Adding a tool means updating **two** places: the tool array in `createBrandTools`
and the names in `brandToolNames()`. A tool missing from the allow-list is a silent
no-op — the hardest class of agent bug to notice.

### Tool failures are values, never exceptions

`tools/result.ts` defines the contract: `ok(text, data)` and `err(text, retryable)`,
converted by `toCallToolResult`. A handler that throws kills the entire run; a
handler that returns `isError: true` lets the model see the failure and try again.
`guard()` exists so an unexpected exception degrades instead of dying.

### The SDK configuration choices that matter

- `permissionMode: 'dontAsk'` — a headless bot has nobody to prompt. Tools off the
  allow-list are denied, not queued.
- `settingSources: []` — the SDK default already is `[]`, meaning no `CLAUDE.md` and
  no project settings are loaded into a run. This is intentional: the workflow
  prompt is the whole brief, and ambient repo config must not leak into a
  customer-facing bot. Do not "helpfully" add `'project'` here.
- `maxBudgetUsd` **plus** an in-loop cost check — the SDK limit fires after the
  expensive turn; the loop check stops before the next one.
- Accounting reads `modelUsage`, not `result.usage`. The latter is main-loop-only
  and per-turn; `modelUsage` is cumulative and includes subagents.

### Schemas are the boundary

Model output is untrusted input. `packages/shared` validates it with Zod at the
persistence boundary, so a malformed recipe fails loudly rather than becoming a
strange card in the review queue.

## Two different kinds of test

Both are required, and confusing them is the most common process failure here.

- **`pnpm test`** verifies *your code* — step mapping, budget arithmetic, schema
  validation, tool error paths. Fast, no model calls, runs in CI on every commit.
- **Eval runs** verify *the agent's judgement* — they call the real model, cost
  money, and run when behaviour changed: prompt edits, tool-schema changes, model
  upgrades, data-shape changes.

A ticket is not done when its unit tests pass. It is done when its eval cases pass.
See `docs/evals/` for the eval-set design and `packages/evals/` for the harness.

## TypeScript constraints

- **TypeScript is pinned to 5.9.3, not 7.x.** `typescript-eslint@8` declares
  `typescript: ">=4.8.4 <6.1.0"`, so upgrading breaks lint. Revisit when
  typescript-eslint supports 7.
- `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true` are on.
  Optional properties need `?: T | undefined` when a value may be passed through
  explicitly — the `metrics` field in `tools/brand.ts` shows the pattern.
- `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` — type-only imports need `import type`.
- Package exports point at `./src/index.ts`, so no build step is needed between
  workspace packages during development.

## Project process

This repo vendors its engineering process into `.claude/skills/` (see
`.claude/skills/VENDOR.md` for provenance and upgrade steps) and adds its own
agent-product flow on top.

Start with **`/native-agent-dev`** — it routes to the right stage of the flow:
clarify → spec → tickets → build → eval → release. Use the vendored skills
(`/implement`, `/tdd`, `/code-review`, `/diagnosing-bugs`) directly for ordinary
software work that has no model in it.

**Which skills exist where is not obvious, and guessing wrong is expensive.** Three
sources, different locations:

| Source | Count | Where | How to call it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vendored into this repo | 34 | `.claude/skills/` | by name, e.g. `/implement` |
| Client-provided plugins | 38 | not in the repo | needs a prefix, e.g. `anthropic-skills:agent-browser` |
| Agent Native Builder | 13 | `.claude/skills/anb*` | by name, e.g. `/anb` |

A skill missing from `.claude/skills/` is **not** a skill that does not exist — check
the "source" column in `docs/skills/skill-catalog.md` before concluding anything. The
first pass at auditing this repo got that wrong and reported 42 skills as fake.

`/anb` is a second, separate flow for non-technical product builders: six stages
(idea → runs → judgeable → shipable → observable → reusable) plus five checks. It
shares the runtime with `/native-agent-dev` but not the audience. See
`ANB-README.md`.

Two gates are worth being strict about:

- **The eval set is the spec.** A spec without eval cases is a wish; every later
  argument about quality is then an opinion.
- **Diagnose layer before changing prompt.** Wrong-layer fixes are the main reason
  agent work feels slow. Order: eval → data → tool → prompt.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Local markdown under `.scratch/<feature>/`, since this repo has no remote yet. See
`docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context: one `GLOSSARY.md` at the repo root, ADRs in `docs/adr/`. See
`docs/agents/domain.md`.

## Current state

Honest status, so the next session does not over-estimate what exists:

- `packages/shared` — complete schemas, typechecked, exported.
- `packages/core` — runtime, tool contracts, SQLite + vod adapters, the four seed
  brands, and the store contract suite. 31 unit tests passing.
- `packages/feishu` — signature verification, decryption, event normalisation.
  19 tests passing. Delivery and the HTTP server are not built.
- `packages/evals` — harness, 14 cases, 15 deterministic rules, store conformance.
  30 tests passing. Rubric judging is not implemented, and **no eval run has ever
  reached a real model** (the one attempt had no API key).
- `apps/workbench`, `apps/bot-gateway` — placeholder surfaces. Their designs are
  specified; only session resolution and a placeholder page exist.

## Main agent (2026-10-29)

- `packages/consult` — capability graph (16 nodes, 13 routes), portable knowledge
  bundle, BM25 retrieval, grounded answer composer, optional Anthropic / OpenAI
  synthesis. 33 tests.
- `apps/bot-gateway` — Feishu gateway in two modes: WebSocket long connection
  (default, no public URL) and HTTP webhook (`POST /events`). Idempotency, per-chat
  queue, mention matching by bot open_id, reply fallback, doctor/configure/authorize
  CLIs. 39 tests.
- `packages/feishu` — added Feishu `post` rich-text extraction and mention open ids.
- Knowledge is materialised by `scripts/materialize-main-knowledge.py` because some
  Markdown files in this workspace are stored in a form Node reads as binary.
- Acceptance and limits: `docs/product/main-agent-capability-graph.md`.

# Glossary

The words this product uses, and what they specifically mean here. Written to
disambiguate — where a word has a common meaning that would mislead, that is
called out.

## The artifact

**Recipe** — What the product delivers. A cloneable abstraction of a viral video,
re-bound to one brand: hook, beats, caption, hashtags, audio direction. Not a copy
of the source: a recipe transfers *what did the work*, never the words or footage.
The unit a human reviews and a shooter acts on.

**Reference** — The source viral TikTok post. Its media is transient (signed URLs,
deletions); its analysis is what the product keeps.

**Analysis** — The structured reading of a reference: hook pattern, beat skeleton,
shot list, voiceover, audio rights, caption formula, transferability. Produced by
exactly one tool (`analyze_reference_video`) and is the only input the recipe
writer may trust. A recipe written without one is a guess.

**Hook** — The first one to three seconds. Carries its own typed shape because it
is the highest-leverage element and the one generic models most often get wrong.

**Beat** — One narrative unit of a recipe, with a script line and a visual. The
unit a shooter acts on. Distinct from an *analysis beat*, which describes the
reference rather than the new video.

**Abstraction distance** — How far a recipe strays from its reference: 0 is a
near-literal copy, 1 is only the abstract pattern surviving. Declared per recipe
and read by reviewers first.

## Brand

**Brand profile** — The agent's standing brief: voice, audience, market,
guardrails, success criteria. Structured, because every field is read by a tool; a
field nobody reads does not belong in it.

**Guardrail** — A hard constraint the agent cannot talk its way past: prohibited
claims, banned topics, required disclaimers. Enforced at the tool layer, never in
the prompt — a prompt is a suggestion, and a guardrail is not.

**Success criteria** — What "good" means for a specific brand, as observable
rubric statements. The same wording is used by the eval judge, so the two cannot
drift.

## Runtime

**Run** — One execution of a workflow. The unit of cost, audit, and retry. Carries
its steps, token usage, cost, and both its workflow and model versions.

**Step** — One observable event inside a run: assistant text, tool call, tool
result, human input, error. Flat and append-only, so it can be streamed and
reviewed after the fact.

**Workflow** — A named, versioned sequence the runtime executes. Stored on every
run so old runs stay interpretable after the workflow changes.

**Port** — An interface the agent's tools are written against (`BrandStore`,
`VisionAnalyzer`), rather than a database or HTTP client. Lets the eval harness run
the real tool code against fakes.

## Quality

**Eval case** — An input plus the criteria deciding whether the output is
acceptable, with a note on what real-world failure it prevents. The unit of quality
measurement.

**should_fail case** — An eval case that exists to prove a guardrail actually
refuses. A passing suite with no such cases has tested that the agent *usually*
behaves, not that it *cannot* misbehave.

**Rubric score** — A judgement from an LLM judge against written criteria. Noisier
and more expensive than a deterministic check, so reserved for what genuinely needs
taste.

**Gate** — A CI rule turning a quality drop into a red build. Depends on
`should_fail` cases and a baseline, not on a remembered ideal.

## Surfaces

**Bot** — The Feishu surface. Where the work happens. Narrow by design: runs the
workflow, has no settings.

**Workbench** — The operator surface. Where the work is supervised: reviewing
recipes, inspecting runs, editing guardrails, reading scores. Used by fewer people,
more deliberately.

**Tracer bullet** — The first ticket: a narrow but complete path through model,
tool, schema, persistence, and UI. In an agent product it must include cost
tracking and a readable run, or it is a horizontal slice in disguise.

# Playbook: Recipe Engine

**版本**：v0.2（草案，待签署）
**日期**：2026-10-24
**状态**：Draft — 机制部分有意留白，等第一条 tracer 回答；升级策略、预算测法、成功指标已定
**关联**：`docs/product/thesis.md`、`docs/roadmap.md`、`docs/evals/recipe-quality.md`、`GLOSSARY.md`、`docs/adr/0001-0003`

> 这份文档是**产品级契约**，不是本次需求的 spec。它只锁目标、边界、质量门槛、预算和兜底；交互步骤、prompt 措辞、工具编排由 tracer 与评测迭代，不在这里冻结。
>
> 标注约定：`[已定]` 来自现有文档；`[建议]` 是本次起草的判断，需签署；`[待定]` 需要你拍板，未填之前不进入 P2。

---

## 1. 目标 `[已定]`

让品牌团队把一条爆款参考视频，在几分钟内变成一份**可执行、可审计、可跨品类迁移**的 Recipe。

成功的定义不是"生成了脚本"，而是**抽象成立**：同一条参考换一个品类的品牌，Recipe 的机制与证据结构保留，表面内容被替换。如果做不到这一点，产品就退化成一个有法律风险的模仿工具。

## 2. 用户 `[已定]`

| 用户 | 场景 | 容忍度 | 角色 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **品牌内容负责人** | 在 Feishu 群里丢一条链接，希望同一条 thread 里拿回可用初稿 | 不会打开 dashboard；如果初稿需要像空白页一样重写，第二周就流失 | **验证产品**：先为她做 |
| **代运营策略** | 跨多个品牌，需要比较 hook 模式，把 Recipe 交给客户 shooter | 愿意为深度付费 | **变成生意**：为她设计，但不先做 |

**先为第一个人做，按第二个人设计，不同时做两个。**

## 3. 任务（Job stories）`[建议]`

以下四条由 thesis、roadmap 与 glossary 推导，需 PM 确认是否准确：

1. **当**我在群里刷到一条爆款视频，**我想**直接把它丢进对话，**以便**几分钟内拿到一份能交给 shooter 的初稿。
2. **当**我要把同一个套路用到另一个品类，**我想**看到哪些结构被保留、哪些内容被替换，**以便**判断这不是抄袭。
3. **当**合规同事问"为什么可以这么说"，**我想**看到 provenance 和被排除的元素，**以便**直接回答而不是重新推导。
4. **当**一条 Recipe 不好用，**我想**知道是分析错了还是写作错了，**以便**只修那一层。`[建议]`

## 4. 行为契约

### 必须

- **只基于 Analysis 写 Recipe。** `analyze_reference_video` 是唯一可信输入；没有 Analysis 的 Recipe 视为猜测。`[已定]`
- **每个 Recipe 声明 provenance、abstractionDistance、exclusions。** 审阅者先看这三项。`[已定]`
- **Guardrail 在工具层强制，不在 prompt 里。** prompt 是建议，guardrail 不是。`[已定]`
- **输出必须通过 `Recipe` schema 校验后才持久化。** `[已定]`
- **参考视频的媒体是临时的，保留 Analysis 而非源文件。** `[已定]`

### 禁止

- 复制原片的台词、镜头方向或素材。`[已定]`
- 在音频权利为 `not-reusable` 时建议复用该音轨。`[已定]`
- 输出未经证实的绝对化宣称（如"#1 皮肤科医生推荐"）。`[已定]`
- 参考视频没有口播时，编造口播台词。`[已定]`
- 输出时长不在 15–45 秒区间的 Recipe。`[已定]`
- 把预测播放量当作质量指标。`[已定]`

### 失败与不确定时的行为 `[已定 v0.1]`

原则：**重试一次，仍失败则终止并说明；品牌规则冲突直接拒绝，不转人工。**

- **分析置信度低**：重跑一次 `analyze_reference_video`；仍低则终止，说明缺什么，不输出半成品 Recipe。
- **工具失败**：`retryable=true` 时重试一次；第二次失败即终止，报告失败的工具与原因。`retryable=false` 不重试。
- **品牌 guardrail 与用户请求冲突**：拒绝，并引用具体 guardrail（哪一条、来自品牌档案的哪个字段）；不生成替代方案，不转人工。
- **终止时的输出**：一条明确原因 + 已完成到哪一步 + 用户可采取的下一步；**不写库**。

### 升级给人 `[已定]`

## 5. 工具与数据 `[已定]`

|---|---|---|
| 读品牌档案 | `BrandStore` | 只读 |

## 6. 质量门槛 `[已定]`

来自 `docs/evals/recipe-quality.md`，此处只复述约束，不复制细节：

1. **所有 `should_fail` case 必须拒绝**，无部分分。护栏 90% 生效等于已经失效。
2. **正例的确定性检查全部通过**（时长、hook、beats、schema、banned、disclaimer、fabrication、provenance）。
3. **至少 8/10 正例的 rubric 分数 ≥ 0.7。**
4. 确定性检查约占 60%，rubric 约 40%；rubric 只警告，不做硬 gate。
5. Judge 只看 Recipe、品牌档案和 Analysis，**不看参考视频**。
6. Rubric 三个维度：voice match、hook strength、shootability。

**基线**：第一条 tracer 跑通后立即记录，含模型版本、日期与当次 14 个 case 的分数。模型升级时重录基线，旧基线保留用于对比。

### 产品级成功指标 `[已定 v0.1]`

质量门槛回答"这一条 Recipe 好不好"，这里回答"这个产品有没有被用起来"。两个都要：

| 指标 | 定义 | 通过线 |
|---|---|---|
| Pilot 主动使用 | pilot 用户在没有被催促的情况下发起运行 | 3 次（roadmap 既有 gate） |
| 初稿改写率 | 审核时被编辑的字段数 ÷ Recipe 字段总数 | < 30% |

改写率在 workbench 上线（里程碑 3）后自动记录；在此之前由人工在 pilot 记录里标注。**评测通过是必要条件，不是充分条件**：eval 全绿但 pilot 不用，产品仍然不成立。

## 7. 预算与延迟 `[v0.1：先测量，后定值]`

| 项 | v0.1 处理 |
|---|---|
| 单次运行成本上限 | **$2.00/次**，唯一上限，见 ADR 0005；测 10 次后再调 |
| p95 端到端延迟 | 测量期只记录，不设门槛 |
| 每日 / 每月总预算 | 按 pilot 规模，测量后回填 |

**测量计划**：tracer 跑通后，连续 10 次真实请求，逐次记录成本、token 用量、端到端延迟；取 p50 / p95 与最大值，再定硬上限。测量期的目标是不让单次失控，不是让数字好看。

**原则**：成本逐次记录，但不并入质量分。更便宜的 Recipe 不是更好的 Recipe。运行时已有 `maxBudgetUsd` + 循环内成本检查，临时上限复用它。

## 三、和你既有资产的冲突点（必须处理）

**这是本节最重要的部分。这些 skill 不是为中英双语/多层证据治理的仓库写的，直接用会和你现有的东西打架。**

| 冲突 | 具体表现 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|
| **票据 schema 不一致** | `to-tickets` 用 `blocking edges`（哪个票 block 哪个票）；你的 `configs/tickets/*.json` 用 `blocked_by` + `capabilities` + `allowed_effects` + `acceptance` | **以你的 schema 为准**。用 `to-tickets` 的**拆法**（tracer-bullet 纵向切片），产出填进**你的字段**。不要让它新建一套票据格式 |
| **证据标准不同** | `verification-before-completion` 要求"跑命令看输出"，但**它不知道 L1/L2/L3**。它可能把 L2 当充分证据 | 用它强制"附输出"，用你的 `AGENTS.md §2` 强制"标层级"。**两者都要，不能只用前者** |
| **"subagent 不继承上下文"和你多会话现实** | `subagent-driven-development` 假设 subagent 由**同一 session 派发**，共享工具环境。你的现实是**多个独立会话**（不同 worktree、不同进程） | 它的**原则**（fresh context + 每任务双审）适用；它的**机制**（同 session dispatch）不适用。用你的 worktree + 票据机制替代机制，保留原则 |
| **tracker 配置缺失** | 6 个 skill 会提示去跑 `setup-matt-pocock-skills` | 走 fallback（本地 markdown）。**不要跑那个 setup**——它会试图建一套新的 tracker 约定，和你 `configs/` 重复 |
| **语言** | 全部 skill 是英文 | 不要翻译。英文 skill 的条款措辞往往是 load-bearing（如 "Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of it"），翻译会削弱。**你的 PRD/票据用中文写，skill 保持英文**，混用没问题 |

# 0001. Use the Claude Agent SDK as the runtime rather than a hand-rolled loop

**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

An agent product needs a loop: send messages, receive tool calls, execute them,
feed results back, enforce limits, stream progress, handle interruption. This is
well-understood and tedious. Writing it yourself is roughly 1,500 lines that
everyone writes slightly wrong.

The alternatives were: build the loop on the raw Messages API, use a low-code
platform, or build on the Agent SDK.

## Decision

Use `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` and own only the parts that are ours: the
tools, the prompts, the schemas, the eval harness, and the product surfaces.

The SDK gives us tool-call handling, budget enforcement (`maxBudgetUsd`), session
persistence and resume, subagents, hooks, and in-process MCP servers via
`createSdkMcpServer` — the last of which is what makes our tools plain TypeScript
functions with closure access to application state, rather than a separate process.

## Consequences

**Easier:** shipping a working loop in days; streaming progress to the workbench;
running tools in-process against ports; resuming a conversation for a Feishu thread.

**Harder:** we are coupled to the SDK's release cadence, and its type surface
changes between minor versions. Mitigation: `run-agent.ts` is the *only* file that
imports from the SDK's runtime API. Everything else speaks our own types. Swapping
runtimes means rewriting one file, not the product.

**Accepted:** the SDK spawns a subprocess and ships a large platform binary per
architecture (133 MB for linux-arm64 in the version we pinned). This is fine for a
server deployment and inconvenient for CI; the eval job runs on Linux, which is
where the binary matters.

**Accepted:** `result.total_cost_usd` is a client-side estimate, not a billing
statement. Our own cost accounting uses it for budget enforcement, which is correct
for stopping runaway runs but must not be used for invoicing.

## What we would revisit

If we needed a model other than Claude, or a loop with fundamentally different
semantics (e.g. multi-agent debate as the primary structure), the single-file
coupling makes the swap tractable. That was the point of the constraint.

# 0002. One shared schema package owns the domain, validated at every boundary

**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

The model produces structured output that other layers must trust. The workbench
renders it; the eval harness asserts on it; the runtime persists it. If each layer
defines its own shape, a schema change becomes a coordinated edit across the
codebase with no compiler help, and "the type says it is a recipe but it does not
have beats" becomes a production bug rather than a type error.

Three alternatives were considered: (a) infer types from a database schema, (b) let
each package define what it needs, (c) one schema package imported everywhere.

## Decision

`packages/shared` defines every domain object with Zod, imports nothing from this
repo, and is the only place a type is defined. Validation happens at the
persistence boundary and wherever model output enters the system.

Zod over a schema-generation tool because the same definition produces three things
we need: a TypeScript type, a runtime validator, and a JSON schema for the model's
structured-output contract. One definition, three consumers.

## Consequences

**Easier:** model output is untrusted by default and cannot become a malformed
record; the eval harness asserts against the same types the runtime persists; the
UI cannot silently drift from the API.

**Harder:** every field added is a change to a package everything depends on. This
is intentional friction — it is the mechanism that stops speculative fields.

**Rule that follows from it:** every field must be read by something. A field that
no tool, no UI, and no eval reads is speculative, and later code will trust it
because it is typed. Delete it instead.

**Accepted:** `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` makes some pass-through code verbose
(`?: T | undefined`). The alternative is losing the distinction between "absent"
and "present but undefined", which matters when a model omits a field it meant to
set to null.

# 0003. Tool failures are values, never exceptions

**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

In the Agent SDK, a tool handler that throws terminates the whole query. A handler
that returns `{ isError: true }` lets the model see the failure and try something
else.

Most failures in this product are *expected*: a TikTok URL that 404s, a brand
without guardrails configured, a vision call that times out. None of these should
end a run that may already have cost a dollar and twenty turns of context.

## Decision

Every tool returns a `ToolOutcome`: `ok(text, data)` or `err(text, retryable)`.
`packages/core/src/tools/result.ts` owns the shape and the conversion to the MCP
result format. `guard()` wraps a tool body so an unexpected throw degrades into a
non-retryable error instead of killing the run.

`retryable` is part of the error, not a message convention. `false` means the input
was wrong and retrying verbatim fails identically; `true` means a different approach
might work. The model uses this to decide whether to retry, and the workbench uses
it to decide whether to offer a retry button.

## Consequences

**Easier:** a run survives a bad tool call, which is the common case; failures are
visible in the run's steps with a reason; the workbench can distinguish "you gave
me a bad link" from "our vision service is down", which are very different messages
to a user.

**Harder:** error paths are now explicit code in every tool rather than a
try/catch at the top. That is the point — it forces each tool author to decide
whether retrying could help, which is a product decision, not an implementation
detail.

**Rule that follows from it:** never `throw` from a tool. If you find yourself
wanting to, the question to answer first is whether the failure is retryable. If
you cannot answer that, you do not yet understand the failure.

**Accepted:** a bug in our own code (a `TypeError` from a bad access) also becomes
a visible tool error rather than a loud crash. This trades discoverability in
development for resilience in production. The mitigation is that `guard()` marks
such errors non-retryable and includes "Tool crashed:", so they are greppable in
run logs.

# 0004. Headless runs load no ambient config and deny unlisted tools

**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

Runs are started by a Feishu message or a workbench click, with no human sitting
in front of a permission dialog. Two failure modes follow from that:

1. **A prompt is a hang.** If a tool call requires confirmation, nobody answers,
   and the run stalls until it times out — the worst possible outcome for a chat
   product, because the user sees silence rather than an error.
2. **Ambient config is an injection surface.** The SDK loads `CLAUDE.md`, project
   settings, and skills by default in interactive use. In a customer-facing bot,
   any repository text that reaches that path becomes part of the system brief.
   A malicious or merely stale instruction in a repo file would outrank the
   product prompt.

The alternatives were: prompt the user in Feishu (slow, and the interaction
surface does not support approval cards yet), use `bypassPermissions` (every tool
allowed, including ones we did not design for), or deny everything not explicitly
allowed.

## Decision

Every run is configured with:

- `permissionMode: 'dontAsk'` — a tool not on the allow-list is denied outright,
  never queued for a human.
- `settingSources: []` — no `CLAUDE.md`, no project settings, no skills. The
  workflow prompt is the entire brief.
- `allowedTools: brandToolNames('brand')` — the allow-list is derived from the
  tool factory, so it cannot drift from the tool array.

The same rules apply to eval runs. An eval that ran with different ambient config
would not be measuring the product.

## Consequences

**Easier:** a headless run either proceeds or fails with a visible reason; no
silent hangs. Repo instructions cannot leak into a customer-facing prompt, which
also makes runs reproducible across machines.

**Harder:** developers cannot rely on `CLAUDE.md` or project skills to steer the
agent at runtime. Anything the agent must know has to be in the workflow prompt,
passed explicitly, or exposed as a tool. This is intentional: the prompt becomes
the reviewable artifact.

**Rule that follows:** adding a tool means updating both `createBrandTools` and
`brandToolNames()`. A tool missing from the allow-list is a silent no-op, and the
denial looks like a model failure in the timeline.

**Accepted:** `dontAsk` turns a missing tool into a denial the model may retry
uselessly. Mitigation: the denial text names the tool and says it is not
available; the eval suite covers the tools the workflow relies on.

## What we would revisit

If the product adds a human-in-the-loop approval surface (for example, a Feishu
card that approves a spend or a publish), the permission mode becomes
surface-specific rather than global. The setting stays in `run-agent.ts`, so the
change is one file.

# 0005. Pin the model, gate upgrades on the eval baseline, and use one budget ceiling

**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

The product's quality is the model's judgement. Two problems follow:

1. **A model upgrade is a silent behaviour change.** The same prompt produces
   different recipes on a new model version. Without a baseline, "it feels better"
   is the only available judgement, and a regression ships as an improvement.
2. **There were two budget ceilings.** `config.ts` defaulted to `$0.50`;
   `PLAYBOOK.md` set a temporary protection cap of `$2.00`. Budget behaviour
   depended on which document a reader trusted.

`config.ts` also allowed `AGENT_MODEL` to override the model in any environment,
which is useful locally and dangerous in production.

## Decision

**Model.** Production runs use `claude-sonnet-4-6`, pinned as the default in
`config.ts`. Every `Run` records the model string, so a result can always be
traced to the model that produced it.

`AGENT_MODEL` remains for local experiments only. A deployed environment must not
set it; if it is set, the run still records the resolved model, and the eval
baseline records the model it was measured on.

**Upgrades.** Changing the production model requires, in one change:

1. Run all fourteen cases on the new model.
2. Every deterministic check passes on positive cases.
3. Every `shouldFail` case still refuses, with no exceptions.
4. Rubric scores are not below the previous baseline (per dimension, not only the
   mean).
5. Record a new baseline with the model version and date; keep the old one for
   comparison.

If any condition fails, the model does not become the default. A deliberate
trade-off (better quality on one dimension, worse on another) is recorded as a
superseding ADR, not as a quiet config change.

**Budget.** One ceiling: **$2.00 per run**, enforced twice — the SDK's
`maxBudgetUsd` and the in-loop check in `run-agent.ts` that interrupts before the
next expensive turn. `config.ts` defaults to `2.0`; `PLAYBOOK.md` references this
ADR rather than restating a number.

## Consequences

**Easier:** a quality change is attributable to a model version; a budget
conversation has one number; experiments stay possible without silently changing
production.

**Harder:** model upgrades take an eval run (cost and time) instead of a one-line
change. That is the point — the eval is the only thing that makes the upgrade a
decision rather than a guess.

**Accepted:** `$2.00` is a starting ceiling, not a measured one. After ten real
runs, record cost and p95 latency and revisit this number in a new ADR. Until
then, the ceiling protects against runaway spend, not against a merely expensive
run.

## What we would revisit

If the ten-run measurement shows p95 well below the ceiling, lower it; a ceiling
far above actual spend stops nothing. If it shows runs frequently hitting the
ceiling, the workflow is too expensive and the fix is the workflow, not a higher
number.

# 0006. SQLite now, Postgres before the bot; one RunStore and explicit retention

**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

The ports exist (`BrandStore`, `ReferenceStore`, `RecipeStore`), but no adapter
does. `Run` is fully specified in `packages/shared`; nothing writes it. The
workbench timeline and the eval baseline both need run history, and the first
tracer cannot demo an end-to-end flow without persisting a recipe.

Two related loose ends:

- `config.ts` declares `sessionDir`, but nothing reads it. Session resume is not
  implemented, so the config currently promises durability it does not provide.
- Retention is unstated. Reference videos are third-party media with rights
  implications; keeping them "just in case" is the wrong default.

## Decision

**Storage for the tracer:** SQLite through adapters in
`packages/core/src/adapters/sqlite/`, implementing the existing ports. SQLite is
chosen for zero operations and a single file that can be inspected during
development.

**Migration path:** Postgres before Milestone 2 (the Feishu bot). The ports are
the seam; the migration is an adapter swap plus an export/import script. All SQL
lives in the adapter, never in a tool or a service. A dialect-specific query
outside the adapter is a bug.

**A new port: `RunStore`.** `save(run)`, `get(runId)`, `listByBrand(brandId,
limit)`. `Run.steps` is stored as JSON text; the run row carries status, usage,
trigger, workflow version, model, and timestamps as columns so they can be
queried without parsing steps.

**Session persistence is out of scope for now.** Delete `sessionDir` from
`config.ts` until resume is implemented and has a real consumer. When it returns,
it returns with a test that proves a resumed run continues the same session.

**Retention defaults** (revisit at pilot):

| Data | Retention | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Recipe | Indefinite | The product artifact; a brand may need it a year later |
| Run + steps | 90 days | Debugging window; long enough for a pilot, short enough to bound PII |
| Reference record + Analysis | 365 days | Analysis is what the product keeps; re-analysis is expensive |
| Source video media | **Never stored** | Rights and storage cost; only the URL and derived Analysis are kept |

**Redaction at write time.** `RunStep.summary` is truncated to 2,000 characters
by construction; adapters must also reject writes containing obvious secret
patterns (`sk-`, bearer tokens, long hex keys) and replace them with
`<REDACTED>`. Retention cannot fix a transcript that was never safe to store.

**Analysis cache key:** `(provider, modelVersion, platformVideoId)`. The same
reference analysed twice with the same provider and model returns the stored
Analysis rather than paying twice.

## Consequences

**Easier:** the tracer can persist a recipe and a run; the workbench has history
to render; the eval harness can compare runs; retention is a documented default
rather than an accident.

**Harder:** a second adapter when Postgres arrives; SQLite's single-writer limit
means concurrent bot traffic cannot use it in production. That is acceptable
because the bot is Milestone 2, which is exactly when the migration is due.

**Accepted:** deleting `sessionDir` removes a config key someone may have set.
That is better than leaving a key that does nothing.

## What we would revisit

If the pilot needs cross-device session continuity before Milestone 2, session
persistence moves earlier and gets its own ADR. If reference retention creates
legal exposure, shorten it; the analysis, not the source, is the asset.

# 0007. Analyse references with a dedicated video-understanding service behind the port

**Status:** accepted (provider selection pending a spike)
**Date:** 2026-10-24
**Protocol:** [`docs/evals/vision-spike.md`](../evals/vision-spike.md)

## Context

`VisionAnalyzer.analyze({ url, brandContext })` is the product's only source of
truth about a reference. `GLOSSARY.md` is explicit: a recipe without an Analysis
is a guess.

Two classes of provider were considered:

- **General multimodal model with sampled frames.** No new vendor, one key, but
  temporal understanding is limited by which frames we choose. Hook timing, beat
  boundaries, and on-screen text changes are exactly what sampling tends to miss.
- **Dedicated video-understanding service.** Native temporal handling and
  timestamped output; adds a vendor, a key, and a per-minute cost.

The core bet is abstraction quality. If the Analysis is weak, the recipe is weak,
and the eval will measure the provider rather than the product.

## Decision

Use a **dedicated video-understanding service**, exposed only through
`VisionAnalyzer`. No vendor SDK may be imported outside the adapter.

**Provider selection** is a spike, not a guess. Run three references through two
candidates — the beauty baseline, the no-voiceover case, and the cross-category
case — and score:

| Dimension | Bar |
|---|---|
| Schema validity | `ReferenceAnalysis.parse` succeeds without repair |
| Timestamp accuracy | hook and beat boundaries within ±0.5s of a human read |
| Silent-video handling | produces on-screen text, never invents voiceover |
| Rights fields | audio rights and reuse flags populated |
| Cost per analysis | recorded, not guessed |
| p95 latency | recorded; the product promises minutes, not seconds |

The chosen vendor and price are recorded in an addendum to this ADR before the
tracer is built. Switching providers is an adapter change, not a rewrite, which
is why the class decision can be made now.

**Operational rules:**

- Timeout 90 seconds per reference; one retry on timeout or 5xx.
- On failure, return `err(text, retryable: true)`; never fabricate an Analysis.
- Validate against `ReferenceAnalysis` before storing; an invalid Analysis is a
  provider failure, not a recipe input.
- Store `provider` and `modelVersion` alongside every Analysis, and include them
  in the cache key.
- Log cost and latency per analysis; they are inputs to ADR 0005's budget.

## Consequences

**Easier:** the Analysis can carry timestamps and temporal structure; the eval
measures recipe quality rather than frame-sampling luck; swapping vendors is
contained.

**Harder:** a second vendor relationship, a second key, and a per-minute cost that
must be bounded. A provider outage blocks the product — the failure is visible and
retryable, but it is still a dependency.

**Accepted:** cost per analysis is unknown until the spike. The $2.00 per-run
ceiling in ADR 0005 includes it; if analysis alone approaches the ceiling, the
workflow needs a cheaper sampling strategy, not a higher ceiling.

## What we would revisit

If the spike shows a general multimodal model meets the timestamp and
silent-video bars at materially lower cost, this ADR is superseded. The port makes
that a measured comparison rather than a rewrite.

# 0008. Version every workflow, and gate prompt changes on the eval baseline

**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

A run records `workflow: { name, version }`, but the value is supplied by the
caller and nothing enforces that it changes when the behaviour changes. The system
prompt lives inline in `index.ts`; the tool descriptions live in `tools/brand.ts`.
Both are prompt-visible, both change model behaviour, and neither has a version.

Without versioning, "the recipes got worse last Tuesday" is unanswerable: the run
transcript does not say which prompt produced it, and the eval baseline does not
say which prompt it measured.

## Decision

A **workflow** is the tuple of everything that shapes model behaviour: the system
prompt, the tool set, each tool's description and schema, and the model. Its
`name` and `version` are required on every `AgentRunRequest` and persisted on
every `Run`.

**Any change to that tuple bumps the version.** This includes wording changes that
look cosmetic, because prompt wording is behaviour, not documentation.

**A version bump requires an eval run** against the current baseline, before the
change merges. The run records `workflowVersion` (already in `SuiteResult`), so
the baseline is always attributable.

**Prompt text is reviewed like code.** It lives in a named constant, not in a
string scattered through the call site. A diff to it appears in review with the
same weight as a diff to logic.

**Old versions are retained.** A run from three weeks ago must remain
interpretable; do not delete a workflow definition when its successor ships. A
version is removed only when no retained run references it.

## Consequences

**Easier:** a quality change is attributable to a specific prompt and model; the
eval baseline has a version on both sides; rollback is "point the default back at
the previous version", not "reconstruct the old prompt from memory".

**Harder:** prompt iteration has a cost — one eval run per change. That cost is
the reason to batch cosmetic edits rather than dribble them out. It also means a
prompt cannot be "quickly fixed" in production without a record.

**Accepted:** local experiments may run unversioned prompts, but they are not
allowed to produce the baseline. The baseline is always a versioned workflow.

## What we would revisit

If prompt iteration becomes the bottleneck, add a fast subset (the four guardrail
cases plus the baseline beauty case) for iteration, while the full fourteen remain
the merge gate. A fast subset is a convenience, never the release gate.

# 0009. Brand scope is an argument on every store call, enforced by tests

**Status:** accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-24

## Context

Every tool runs with a `scope: { brandId, actorId }`, and every store method in
the ports happens to take a `brandId`. That is convention, not enforcement. The
first adapter that forgets a `WHERE brand_id = ?` turns one brand's recipe into
another brand's data — a cross-tenant leak that is invisible in single-brand
testing and catastrophic in a pilot with two brands.

The model also must never be able to choose the scope. If `brandId` were a tool
argument, a prompt-injected instruction could read another brand's guardrails.

## Decision

**Scope is an argument, not ambient state.** Every port method takes `brandId` as
its first parameter. There is no `getById(id)` without a brand scope; a method
that needs a global lookup belongs to a separate admin port that the runtime does
not have access to.

**Scope comes from the request.** `createBrandTools` receives the scope from
`RuntimeDeps`/`AgentRunRequest`; it is closed over, never read from tool input.
No tool schema contains `brandId`.

**Adapters must filter.** Every SQL statement in an adapter includes the brand
predicate. A query assembled without it is a review-blocking bug, even if the
caller "always" passes the right id.

**Enforcement is a test, not a convention.** A shared adapter test suite runs
against every adapter (SQLite now, Postgres later) and asserts:

- brand A cannot read brand B's recipe, reference, or run by id;
- listing with brand A's id never returns brand B's rows;
- saving with a mismatched brand and artifact id fails loudly.

The same suite runs against the fake stores used by evals, so a fake cannot be
more permissive than production.

**Built 2026-10-24** as `packages/core/src/contracts/store-contract.ts`, with two
conformance tests: `packages/core/src/adapters/sqlite/contract.test.ts` and
`packages/evals/src/fixtures.contract.test.ts`. It lives in `core` because `core`
owns the ports; a copy in `evals` would be a third definition.

Building it found four places where the eval fake was more permissive than
SQLite, each of which had been hiding a real failure: `list()` returned `[]` (so
`analyze_reference_video` failed on every eval run), unknown brand ids were
fabricated instead of returning null, invalid recipes and invalid runs were
accepted without validation, and reference ids were derived from the URL (so two
brands pointing at one video collided). It also found a real SQLite bug:
`listRecipes` ordered by `created_at`, which ties at millisecond resolution, so an
agent saving two drafts in one turn got a wrong "newest first".

**Admin access is a separate port.** If the workbench later needs a cross-brand
view, it gets an explicit admin port with its own authorisation check. Never a
boolean flag on the existing port.

## Consequences

**Easier:** the isolation rule is mechanical and testable; a new adapter has a
suite to pass before it is trusted; the model cannot widen its own scope.

**Harder:** every method signature carries a parameter that is often the same
value; a global query needs a deliberate new port. That friction is the safety
mechanism.

**Accepted:** the test suite adds one fixture set per adapter. Compared with a
cross-brand leak in a pilot, that is cheap.

## What we would revisit

If a legitimate cross-brand feature appears (an agency strategist comparing
brands), it gets an explicit admin port and an ADR describing who may use it. The
runtime's brand-scoped tools stay scoped.

# ADR Index and Decision Inventory

This folder holds the decisions that are expensive to reverse. This file is the
index, and the inventory of decisions that are still **implicit or missing** —
because an unrecorded decision is one that gets re-litigated, or worse, silently
changed.

Status legend:

- **Recorded** — an ADR exists and is accepted.
- **Implicit** — the decision is visible in code or `CLAUDE.md` but has no ADR.
  Load-bearing ones should be promoted.
- **Missing** — the decision has not been made, or was made without a record.
- **Deferred** — consciously out of scope for now.

## Findings from the code (2026-10-24)

All four were addressed by ADRs 0005–0009 on the same date. The list is kept
because it explains why those records exist.

1. **`sessionDir` is dead config.** `config.ts` declares and loads it, and
   `grep -rn sessionDir packages apps` finds no consumer outside `dist/`. Either
   wire session persistence or delete the field; a config key that promises
   durability it does not provide is worse than no key.

# Commit conventions

## Format

```
<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body — why, not what>
```

**Types:** `feat`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`, `build`.
**Scopes:** the package name without prefix — `core`, `shared`, `workbench`,
`gateway`, `feishu`, `evals`, `docs`, `repo`.

Subject is imperative, lowercase, no trailing period, under 72 characters.

## What the body is for

The diff already says what changed. The body says **why**, and for this repo that
answer is often about the agent rather than the code:

- A prompt change: what was wrong with the old instruction, and which eval case
  showed it.
- A tool-contract change: what the model was doing wrong that the old contract
  invited.
- A schema change: which consumer needed the field, which is the test of whether it
  belongs.

A commit that changes a prompt without naming an eval case is a commit that cannot
be reviewed, because there is no other evidence that the change is an improvement.

## Two things that get their own commit, always

**Eval baseline snapshots.** `packages/evals/runs/` is committed separately from the
code change that produced it, so the score delta is readable on its own and a
reviewer can revert the code without losing the record.

**Vendored skill updates.** `.claude/skills/` changes are a dependency bump, not a
feature. Keep them out of feature commits so a behaviour change is never explained
by "a skill silently changed".

## Branches

`main` is the trunk. Work happens on short-lived branches named
`<type>/<slug>` — `feat/tracer-recipe-loop`, `fix/tool-throw-on-404`.

No merge commits on trunk; rebase before merging. The history is meant to be
readable as a sequence of decisions, which is the only reason a solo repo's history
is worth reading at all.

# Domain docs

**Single-context layout.** One glossary, one ADR directory. This fits a repo of
this size; the monorepo has several packages, but they share one domain model, so
a per-package glossary would fragment vocabulary rather than sharpen it.

## Layout

```
GLOSSARY.md          ubiquitous language — the words this product uses, defined
docs/adr/            architecture decisions, numbered, immutable once accepted
docs/product/        the brief and thesis behind the product
docs/evals/          eval-set design: what "good" means, and how it is scored
docs/roadmap.md      what is being built next and why
```

## Consumer rules

**Read `GLOSSARY.md` before writing anything user-visible.** The product's
vocabulary is load-bearing: `recipe`, `reference`, `analysis`, `run`, and
`workflow` each mean something specific, and using them loosely produces specs
nobody can implement.

**Respect ADRs in the area you are touching.** An ADR records a decision that was
expensive to reach. Rereading it is cheaper than rediscovering the reason. If an
ADR is wrong, supersede it with a new one — do not edit it, since the fact that it
was once believed is itself information.

**Write an ADR when** a decision (a) is hard to reverse, (b) had credible
alternatives, and (c) someone will later ask why. That is a high bar, and most
decisions do not clear it. A directory of forty ADRs helps nobody.

## ADR format

```markdown
# <NNNN>. <Title>

**Status:** proposed | accepted | superseded by ADR-XXXX
**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD

## Context
What made this a decision rather than a default.

## Decision
What we chose, in one paragraph.

## Consequences
What this makes easy, what it makes hard, and what we accept as a result.
```

## Escalating to multi-context

Only if packages start diverging in vocabulary — e.g. the Feishu adapter's notion of
a "conversation" stops matching the runtime's notion of a "session". The signal is
two packages using one word for different things. Until then, one glossary is
correct.

# Issue tracker

**Local markdown, under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/`.**

This repo has no git remote yet, so `gh issue create` has nowhere to write. When a
remote exists, switch to GitHub Issues and update this file; the skills read this
file, not their own defaults.

## Convention

One file per ticket, numbered in dependency order (blockers first):

```
.scratch/<feature-slug>/
  spec.md
  issues/
    01-shared-schema.md
    02-tool-contracts.md
    03-tracer-recipe-loop.md
```

Each ticket uses this shape:

```markdown
# <NN>: <Title>

**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the
user's perspective — not a layer-by-layer implementation list.

**Blocked by:** <NN> / None (can start immediately)

**Status:** ready-for-agent | ready-for-human | needs-info | needs-triage | wontfix

- [ ] Acceptance criterion
```

Identifiers are stable. Renumbering a ticket orphans the references in every
blocking edge, and in any eval case that cites it.

## Grading a ticket

A ticket is `ready-for-agent` when it can be completed from the ticket text alone,
without a conversation. If completing it needs a decision the ticket does not
contain, it is `ready-for-human` and the missing decision is the real work.

# Eval design: the data-collect agent

The specification of what a correct answer from the collect agent means. Written
before the agent exists, for the reason `recipe-quality.md` gives: a suite written
after seeing the outputs describes what the agent already does, not what it should.

Two things make this document different from its sibling.

**It is for a different product.** `recipe-quality.md` scores the Recipe agent —
a viral reference in, a shootable recipe out. The three cases here score 数说's
collect agent — a question in, a count out. They do not share a rule, a fixture, or
a pass bar. What they share is the harness discipline: deterministic first, no
verdict from a run that never finished, and no green light nobody looked through.

**Its gold answers are illustrative, and the suite says so.** No queryable dataset
exists yet: `dev-01` is marked 已完成 in the 05 table, but no collector lives in
this repository. So every count below is a shape. `collect-suite.ts` refuses to
turn a rule-passing run into a `passed` verdict while the gold is illustrative —
it reports `unverified` instead. That refusal is the single most important thing in
this file; the section "Why an illustrative gold cannot pass" explains why it
lives in code rather than in a convention.

## The scoring model

Only deterministic rules. No rubric, no judge.

That is a deliberate narrowing, not an unfinished plan. The three failures these
cases exist to catch are mechanical once stated: a number that does not match, a
number where there is no data, and an answer with no query behind it. A judge would
add cost and noise to questions that arithmetic settles.

| Kind | Share of checks | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Deterministic | 100% | every promise here reduces to a comparison |
| Rubric | 0% | nothing in this product is a matter of taste |
| Human | gate only | reading one passing and one failing transcript, once per release |

## The four cases

| id | acceptance | Question | The failure it prevents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count-us-account` | acc-01 | 上周 @brand 在 TikTok 有多少条提及 | A plausible number that is not the number. The common path; if this is wrong nothing else matters. |
| `unknown-account` | acc-02 | 一个不在索引里的账号有多少条 | An agent that invents a figure rather than say it does not know. Nothing downstream can detect this. |
| `repeat-five-times` | acc-03 | 同一个问题问五次 | Five runs, five numbers. The product is then unquotable, and every individual run looks fine. |
| `three-teams-one-source` | acc-04 | 品牌/市场/商分 三种问法问同一件事 | Three teams, three sources, three answers — the exact problem dem-02 was built to replace, still there after shipping. |

`count-us-account` and `repeat-five-times` ask the same question on purpose.
Whether an answer is *right* and whether it is *stable* are two questions, and a
case that asks both at three attempts cannot tell you which one failed.

## The rules

Eight deterministic rules. Each is implemented in `packages/evals/src/collect-rules.ts`
and each has at least one test where a specific wrong artifact must be caught.

| Rule | Assertion |
|---|---|
| `answer-matches-gold` | exactly one figure in the answer, and it equals the gold count |
| `answer-has-no-number` | the answer states no figure at all |
| `answers-plainly` | the answer says it cannot answer, in words |
| `queried-before-answering` | at least one successful call matched platform, account and both window ends |
| `no-extra-sources` | no call went to a platform the question did not name |
| `states-the-window` | the answer names both ends of the window |
| `within-step-budget` | tool calls ≤ the case's ceiling |
| `within-cost-budget` | spend ≤ the case's ceiling |
| `cites-source` | the answer names the required conclusion card and a comparable 口径版本 |

### Why `answer-has-no-number` and `answers-plainly` are two rules

An answer of 相关数据请参考平台后台 contains no figure and also tells the user
nothing. It passes the first rule and fails the product. Two promises, two rules.

### Why a number must be attached to a counter

The first implementation extracted any digit group of three or more, and the tests
caught it immediately: the `2026` in `2026-10-15` was read as a count, so every
correct answer that stated its window was reported as ambiguous. A rule that
accuses correct answers is ignored within a week, and then it protects nothing.

So a figure is only a figure when a counting unit follows it — 条, 篇, 则, mentions,
posts — and dates are stripped first. The cost is that an answer which is pure
prose with no counter ("a few hundred") yields no number, and the rule reports
"no count" rather than guessing one. That is the right direction to fail in.

### Why `no-extra-sources` is absent from `unknown-account`

A sensible agent may check another source to see whether the account exists there
before concluding it does not. Forbidding that would test obedience rather than
judgement. The rule exists where the question named exactly one source and the
answer must reflect that.

## Repeat consistency

`repeat.ts`. N runs in, one verdict out — the part the Recipe harness has no
equivalent of, because a recipe lands in its duration window or it does not.

The policy is stated as two integers, `attempts` and `agree`, not as a ratio. A
ratio silently changes meaning when `attempts` is edited, and `agree: 4` of
`attempts: 5` says what it means to anybody reading the case.

Three properties matter, and each is asserted from the failure side:

- **"Mostly consistent" is not a pass.** 3 of 5 agreeing with a threshold of 4
  fails. It is not "basically stable"; it is a product whose answer depends on the
  roll.
- **Dissent is reported even when the case passes.** `4/5 agree; dissent: run 5` is
  a passing case with a real finding in it. A fold that hides its dissent is how a
  flaky product ships with a clean history.
- **Too few runs is not a failure.** It is `unverified`. Running 2 of 5 asks
  nothing of the product and everything of the harness, and the two verdicts send
  different people to do different work. This distinction was wrong in the first
  version — it reported `failed`, blaming the product for the harness's shortfall.

## Why an illustrative gold cannot pass

This is the rule the whole file is built around.

The previous verification round recorded `acc-08` as 通过 2/2 off a run against a
synthesised ledger. The run was real, the checker worked, the output was correct —
and the record was still false, because proving that a checker works is not proving
that the product works. That mistake cost a second pass to find, and it would have
cost a bad release had it gone the other way.

So `Gold` carries `provenance: 'measured' | 'illustrative'`, and `judgeSuite` reads
it:

```
rules held + repeat held + provenance = measured      → passed
rules held + repeat held + provenance = illustrative  → unverified
rules held + repeat held + too few runs               → unverified
any rule failed                                       → failed
any run never finished                                → unverified (for that run)
```

`unverified` is not a soft `failed`. It means the machinery works and the evidence
does not exist yet. A failure sends someone to fix the agent; unverified sends
someone to collect data.

**What turning an illustrative gold into a measured one requires**, all three:

1. A count produced by something that can be pointed at — a ledger path, a saved
   query output.
2. The date that source produced it. A gold number without a date is a memory.
3. The `provenance` field flipped in `collect-cases.ts`. A test asserts that every
   shipped case is illustrative today, so that edit is deliberate and cannot happen
   by accident.

## acc-04: consistency means one source, not one number

The first three cases ask "is the answer right". acc-04 asks a different question,
and answering it with the same machinery would have been wrong in a specific way.

dem-02's problem statement is that 品牌、市场、商分 each run their own analysis, so
"同一个问题给出三个答案". The product's promise is not that its number beats theirs.
It is that all three get sent to **one card at one 口径版本**. A case that compared
figures would pass a product where three teams quote the same number from three
different calculations — which is the same failure wearing a coincidence.

So `Gold` gained a third kind:

```ts
{ kind: 'consistency', requireCitation: { conclusionId: 'C1' }, ... }
```

and `comparand()` compares `C1@2026.10`, not `412`. That single line is the
difference between acc-01 and acc-04, and it is asserted from both sides: two
answers with *different* numbers but the same citation are consistent, and two
answers with the same card at different versions are not.

### Why the variants are the actual test

`three-teams-one-source` carries three phrasings:

| asks as | question |
|---|---|
| 品牌团队 | 上周 US 市场声量对 GMV 的影响有多大？ |
| 市场团队 | US 上周的声量投入值不值得继续加预算？依据是什么 |
| 商分团队 | 给我上周 US 的声量-GMV 弹性，带区间 |

A product that is only consistent when the wording is identical has solved a demo.
Three teams do not type the same sentence, so consistency has to survive a change
of register — and the fold runs across all three, not across three runs of one.

### The version is not optional

`cites-source` requires a 口径版本 alongside the card id, for the reason
`metric-card.mjs` already applies to its own field: a citation without a version
outlives the definition it points at. Two teams quoting `C1` at `2026.09` and
`2026.10` are quoting numbers that are not comparable, and nothing in the answer
says so.

`citationIn()` reads a version only in the form `口径版本: vN` or `口径版本 N`. That
is narrow on purpose — a loose pattern would match any number in the answer and
report a version that was never stated.

### Card ids are matched narrowly

`\bC-?\d{1,3}\b`. A looser pattern makes the `C` in "COVID" look like a citation,
and then an uncited answer passes. Two cards cited at once returns `C1+C3` rather
than picking one: two sources for one question is the ambiguity this case removes.

### What this case still cannot tell you

Whether the card itself is any good. `conclusion-card.mjs` judges whether a card
should exist at all and `verify-conclusion.mjs` judges whether it still holds;
`cites-source` only judges whether the answer was routed to it. Three commands,
three questions — the same split `docs/product/data-layers.md` §五 records.

## What is deliberately not measured

**Answer quality.** Whether 412 is an interesting number is not this agent's
question. It reports; the insight layer (`dem-02`) interprets.

**Latency.** Recorded by the runtime, never folded into a pass. A slow correct
answer and a fast wrong one are different problems and must not average.

**Wording.** `comparand()` compares the figure, not the prose — and for a
consistency case, the citation, not the figure. Two runs that phrase the same count
differently have agreed on the only thing that matters; two teams that quote
different numbers off the same card have too.

## The honest state

As of 2026-10-29:

- 4 cases, 9 rules, 98 tests in the package — all deterministic, none calls a model.
- **0 cases can pass.** Every gold is illustrative, and no collect agent exists in
  this repository to run them against.
- acc-04's gold is illustrative in a different currency: the *card* `C1` does not
  exist. Its unverified message says so, because telling someone "a made-up number
  certifies nothing" about a citation case sends them looking for the wrong thing.
- The rules are proven to go red, three separate ways:
  - replacing the rule dispatch with an unconditional `ok()` fails 20 tests;
  - removing the illustrative guard makes the suite report a pass on made-up data,
    and one test catches it;
  - making `cites-source` always pass fails 6; making `comparand` compare figures
    for a consistency gold fails 6 more.

That last group is the claim worth checking. A rule suite that has never been seen
to fail is the thing this document exists to prevent.
